newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela bolivar ends flat in quieter trade.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela bolivar ends flat in quieter trade.

text.p: The Venezuelan bolivar closed flat at 494.50/495.50 per dollar Tuesday in a market described by traders as much quieter and less volatile following new trading regulations announced by the Central Bank Monday.
"The market stayed around 494/495 bolivars all day. From here it looked very quiet with little demand," one trader said.

Moves by the Central Bank Monday to slow the depreciation rate of its bands system, drain excess liquidity from money markets and restrict the use of interbank currency trading, had calmed the market, traders said.
The Central Bank did not have to supply as much currency to the market as in recent sessions, the added.

Currency markets were seen even quieter Wednesday with little price fluctuations with many traders not sure whether clients or banks would be working due to a 12-hour national work stoppage called by unions.

Venezuela's foreign exchange market is unusual in that the Central Bank is its largest single supplier of dollars, which blurs the difference between the Central Bank supplying liquidity and intervening.
